quotes.text: Decisions don't need adrenaline, they need reproducibility. If you can't rerun the same query tomorrow and get the same answer for yesterday, you don't have analytics, you have gossip.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines reproducibility as the real requirement behind trustworthy analytics.

quotes.text: Stability beats recency for decision making. Not always, but whenever money, compliance, or accountability is involved, you need the exact same answers tomorrow that you saw today for the same timestamped reality.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core principle of the episode and when it applies.

quotes.text: Snapshots are a protocol for operational truth. A handshake between engineering, analytics, and compliance that says, this is the state we all agree on.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Positions snapshots as an agreement between teams rather than a technical toggle.

quotes.text: If you mix snapshot tables with live tables in one report, you reintroduce ambiguity. If you let anyone roll snapshots forward before validation's pass, you're back to chaos in a nicer outfit.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the two most common mistakes that undo the benefit of snapshots.

quotes.text: If you remember nothing else, remember this. Truth is a timestamp you can name, not a vibe you can feel.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable one-line summary of point-in-time analytics.

takeaways: Querying a warehouse while ETL is running produces numbers that change mid-meeting; read replicas only copy that volatility, they do not freeze it.
Fabric warehouse snapshots give a read-only, transactionally consistent, zero-copy point-in-time view that you capture before loads and roll forward only after validation passes.
Combine named snapshots for month-end and audits with RBAC, Purview sensitivity labels, audit logs and a snapshot catalog to get reproducible, governed reporting.
hook: Dashboards that shift while ETL runs leave executives asking which number is right. This episode is for data engineers, BI developers and finance analysts working with Microsoft Fabric. It shows how warehouse snapshots deliver one stable, auditable version of truth for month-end close, daily reporting and audit replay.
